title: Implement Stack Using Queues

contractDetails.constraints: At most 100 method calls. 1 ≤ x ≤ 9. pop and top only occur when nonempty. Rows [0,x], [1], [2], [3] mean push, pop, top, empty. Construct once and serialize only the last three methods, encoding booleans as 0 or 1.
contractDetails.output-checking: Construct MyStack once. [0,x] calls push, [1] pop, [2] top, [3] empty. Serialize non-void returns in order. Encode bool returns as integer 0 or 1.

statement: Implement MyStack using queue operations. push(x) adds the newest value, pop() removes and returns it, top() reads it, and empty() reports whether no values remain. A queue may only append at the back, read/remove at the front, and report size or emptiness.

examples.explanation: The latest pushed value leaves first.
The empty state changes across calls.
Repeated values are separate stack entries.

constraints: At most 100 method calls. 1 ≤ x ≤ 9. pop and top only occur when nonempty. Rows [0,x], [1], [2], [3] mean push, pop, top, empty. Construct once and serialize only the last three methods, encoding booleans as 0 or 1.
hints: Conceptual: A queue removes the oldest value, while a stack needs the newest.
Directional: Reorder the queue after each insertion.
Implementation: After enqueueing the new value, move every older queued value from front to back. The new value is now at the front.
complexityAnalysis: push is O(n), pop/top/empty are O(1), and storage is O(n).
